children: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Ltd. Sponsored ADR (TWSE:2330) is expanding capacity and advanced packaging—building four 1.4nm fabs and two packaging sites—while rolling out N2P IP, Cadence tool certifications and possible 3%–6% wafer price hikes as it readies Q3 results amid volatile trading.
: TSMC (2330) will build four 1.4nm fabs in Central Taiwan, aiming for 120,000–160,000 12" wafers monthly and $45–$52B annual revenue contribution.
: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (2330) will report Q3 results the week of Oct. 12–16. Traders may watch earnings timing and stock's beta-linked return behavior during that busy week.
: TSMC (2330) reportedly plans wafer price hikes of about 3%–6% from January 2027, with bigger increases for advanced processes, per DigiTimes-sourced report; company gave no comment.
: TSMC (2330) taped out N2P IP including DDR5, LPDDR5 and PCIe 6.0; PCIe 3.0 IP expected Q4 2026. UCIe-64G on N2P tested and characterized for AI infrastructure.
: Cadence certified tools for TSMC (2330) A16 and A14 nodes, covering digital flow, signoff, and analog; listed tools enable AI and high-performance computing design support.
: TSMC (2330) enabled TSMC-COUPE integration with Cadence 224G SerDes IP, aligning it with UALink, ESUN, UltraEthernet and CPO ecosystems to support HPC and AI applications.

: TSMC (2330) is building two advanced-packaging facilities and a training center at Kaohsiung’s Baipu park, aiming to start operations in Q4 2029; company says the hub may boost validation efficiency.
: TSMC ADR (2330) fell about 1% to $442.29 at 10:17 a.m. ET after news tied to its Kaohsiung hub.
This is an AI-generated summary and may contain inaccuracies. Please verify any important information with the original sources.

title: Weekly Recap: 1.4nm fab buildout and Q3 earnings week, beta-linked returns
